frames.review_note: Minor only. The r1 failures are fixed: the brand and the thin white scar are now on the LEFT forearm draped over the horse's neck, the near right forearm is unmarked, and the hooves are solid. Nagoji matches the sheet and the bible: rust-red turban, clear grey at the temple, thick curled moustache, chin clean apart from faint shading, small gold stud, sleeves pushed up, boots. The grey horse with the black mane lies with his head down in the straw, and the two grooms hang back at the sunlit doorway. Small nits: the horse lies half on his chest rather than flat on his side, there is a tiny mark on Nagoji's cheek by the eye, and the brand shows on the upper face of the draped forearm. The single caption fits on the slatted wall at upper centre.

Clean close insert, as the r1 correction asked. It shows a LEFT hand lying flat on the grey neck under the black mane (palm down, thumb on the right, five sound digits) and the cream sleeve pushed up. The brand is a small round puckered patch with no letters and no cross, and the thin white scar runs beside it toward the elbow. The stable slats, trough and warm dawn stripes match 1.1. Nit: with the palm down, the brand sits on the upper face of the forearm rather than strictly the inner side, the same placement as 1.1, so the page stays consistent. Both captions fit in the upper-left wall and slat area.

Clean, and the r1 failures are fixed: the shot is tight on the grey horse's half-closed eye with still lashes and black forelock strands, straw below, and the edge of Nagoji's hand at the right frame edge. No face, no blue coat, no grooms. The warm dawn slat light matches 1.1 and 1.2. The caption fits in the upper-left stable-wall corner or over the dark mane along the top.

Minor: the sun already sits just above the hills, so the light reads closer to sunset than late afternoon; the hoe blade is angled to the shaft but reads somewhat like a spade. On model otherwise: rust-red turban, red sash as in 1.1, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, grey at the temple, brand and white scar correctly on the inner LEFT forearm, lone tamarind with pods, long grave cut in red earth, estate roofs and drill ground far below. No lettering needed.

Acceptable, and all r1 failures are fixed: rust-red turban as in 1.4, small gold stud, raw blistered PALMS turned toward the viewer, and a long human shadow across the mound from off panel. Moustache, clean chin, clear grey at the temple, red sash, talwar at the left hip and boots are all correct. Tamarind, red laterite mound, estate roofs and drill ground below match the setting, and the open sunset sky at upper right is clear for Dhanaji's off-panel balloon. Residual nits for the author: (1) The tool leaning on the trunk has a socketed, in-line blade and reads more like a spade than the angled Kerala mammatty in 1.4, though its wood-and-iron look matches. (2) The brand here is an elongated ridged stripe up the forearm rather than the small round patch plus thin scar of 1.1 and 1.2. (3) The off-panel man stands at the bottom (camera) edge, so his shadow points toward the sun, which is physically off. (4) The red raw palms are close to reading as bloody at small size. The tail points to the bottom edge where the shadow's feet leave the frame.

Minor only. Dhanaji stands a pace or two back by the tamarind trunk, not right at Nagoji's shoulder. The brand on Nagoji's pushed-up LEFT forearm sits nearer mid-forearm than a hand's width above the wrist, with the long white scar beside it, as the bible describes. Everything else matches: Nagoji has the rust-red turban, red sash, grey at the temple, gold stud, thick moustache and clean chin, and he does not look up. Dhanaji has the white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short black beard and talwar. The sunset hilltop and mound match 1.5, and there is wide open sky at upper right for both of Nagoji's lines.

Minor: light hatched stubble texture on the cheek and jaw, but the chin reads clean-shaven, with no beard. Matches the beat: a profile against the red sky with tamarind leaves and pods above, the rust-red turban, clear grey at the temple, the thick curled moustache, a flush gold stud and the grave mound visible lower right. The red sash shows as a shoulder drape in this close shot, which matches the diagonal strap in 2.3. No painted text, no hands shown. Clear red sky at upper right (x 0.55 to 0.95, y 0.2 to 0.45) for the balloon near his mouth.

Minor only. Dhanaji's raised counting hand is lit against the sky rather than truly silhouetted. It shows a thumb and three fingers, with the little finger hidden or folded, which still reads as counting. The training-ground lamps are open-flame lamps on posts, not glass lanterns. Everything else matches: Nagoji in the rust-red turban is on the far side, with grey at the temple, gold stud and clean chin. Dhanaji in the white pagdi, indigo tunic and short beard is on the near side. The evening drill is forming up below with lamps lit, and there is clear sky at top centre and right for both balloons.

Minor only. The recruit reads as pouring from his powder flask, with powder heaped on the ground, rather than as having just spilt it, though the beat still lands with the veteran pointing and bellowing. In the background kalari, one pair's sticks cross a little awkwardly. The tall banner is plain white cloth with no lettering. Daylight and the kalari pit with its lamp shrine are correct, the period flintlocks and powder flasks are fine, there is no text, and there is a large clear sky at top centre for the caption.

Minor: faint stubble hatching on the jaw, but the chin reads clean-shaven. The close shot on Nagoji looking down toward the lamp-lit drill ground at dusk matches 2.3 (the same tiled estate, torches and drilling ranks). The grey at the temple is clearly drawn and the gold stud is flush on the lobe. No painted text, no gore, no hands in frame. Captions can sit in the open dusk sky at upper right (x 0.5 to 0.98, y 0.12 to 0.36), clear of the face and the drill.

Minor: the pale puckered brand on the left forearm sits closer to the elbow than a hand's width above the wrist, with the long white scar running from it toward the wrist. Otherwise clean: bare-chested, ribs bound in cream cloth, cream dhoti, hair loose, thick curled moustache, clean chin with light stubble, small gold stud, no grey, no sacred thread, eyes on the jackfruit leaves. Both captions fit in the sky and foliage band at top centre.

Minor only. Revathi's forehead shows two short white sandal lines across mid-forehead, not one thin line at the hairline as in panels 3 and 5, and a tiny reddish crease between the brows (about 3x6 px). At reading size it reads as a frown line, not a bindi, but a retouch to skin tone would be safer for the widow rule. Padmini's black hair has more grey streaking than 'a few fine threads', though it fits the ch16 bible row 'grey threading through her black hair'. Everything else is right: Nagoji bare-chested with his ribs bound, cream dhoti, hair loose, no turban, thick moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, no grey, and the brand on his LEFT forearm. Padmini sets the clay pot by the mat with her stick. Revathi sits on the low laterite wall near his feet, eyes on the sky. Same courtyard, jackfruit tree and verandah as panels 3 and 5. No painted text. The caption fits on the tree trunk at top left, and Padmini's balloon fits in the foliage and sky above her head.

Minor only. Revathi's face is turned away, chin on her hand, but her eyes cut sideways toward Nagoji's side, so it reads as a dry side-eye rather than strictly not looking. She has a tiny dark (not red) dot between her brows. The mark on Nagoji's LEFT forearm is drawn as a white looping scar line, not a puckered patch. It is small and does not read as lettering. Otherwise it matches the script: Revathi in the foreground on the low wall in an indigo sari with gold, jasmine braid, coin necklace, armlets and one sandal line at the hairline; Nagoji beyond her on his mat, bare-chested with ribs bound, hair loose, thick moustache, clean chin, gold studs, no grey. Same courtyard as panels 2 and 5. No painted text. The balloons fit in the canopy at top left and in the sky and wall above Nagoji, and the foreground stone ledge is also clear.

Minor: the brand and long scar sit mid-forearm on the arm hanging to the mat, with the hand palm-down. They may read as the outer face of the forearm rather than strictly the inner. The hair has a few silvery highlight strands, but no grey at the temple. Otherwise clean: bare chest, ribs bound, cream dhoti, moustache, clean chin, gold stud. Revathi leans in with both hands at the bandage end at his side, and her costume matches her sheet (no tali). Same courtyard as 3.1. Lettering fits in the sky and foliage above and between their heads.

Minor only. Revathi has a tiny dark dot just above her brow line next to the single sandal line at the hairline, which is barely visible. The lettering space is a little tight. Use the laterite wall and foliage between Revathi's head and Nagoji's hair (about x 0.37 to 0.53, y 0.08 to 0.32) for the medium balloon, and the jackfruit canopy at top left or the verandah roof at top right for the short one. Otherwise it is a strong match: a close shot of Revathi's two well-drawn hands with bangles, pulling the rib bandage tighter; Nagoji's jaw set with his head tilted back against the sting, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold studs, hair loose and black with no grey; the brand patch and the long white scar on his LEFT forearm, exactly as in the bible. Same courtyard and light as panels 2 and 3. No painted text, blood or gore.

Minor only: faint stubble shading on the chin (reads as clean-shaven in ink), and the pale brand/scar marks sit on the top of the left forearm rather than the inner side. A lit brass lamp on the verandah in afternoon light is harmless. Convalescent look correct (bare-chested, ribs bound, cream dhoti, no turban, hair loose, no grey, small gold stud), same courtyard/tree/wall/verandah as page 3. Lettering fits in the sky band between the leaves and the roof (upper middle and upper right).

Minor: Revathi has a tiny pale sandal-coloured dot between the brows in addition to the hairline sandalwood lines (not red, no tali or sindoor); her hands hold the bandage tail beside his left forearm rather than right at the knot, but it reads as tying off. Nagoji chin has faint stubble shading but reads clean-shaven; tiny flush ear stud correct. Same courtyard and costume as 4.1. Two Revathi balloons fit in the sky gap between the two heads and below the leaves.

Minor: a sliver of Revathi's profile edge shows past her raised calling hand, but her face is effectively hidden with her back to us as scripted. A small framed wall fixture by the verandah door is unreadable and carries no text. Nagoji matches (moustache, clean chin, gold stud, bound ribs, cream dhoti, brand marks on left forearm). Same courtyard as 4.1 and 4.2. Balloon can sit in the sky beside Revathi's head; caption in the upper-middle sky below the leaves.

Clean on the essentials. It is a wide-ish, starlit, moonless courtyard with no lamps lit and the jackfruit tree on the left. One figure, Revathi, is on-sheet (indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, gold necklace and armlet, no tali), wrapped in a dark shawl, crossing the paving and carrying no light. The hands are sound and there is no text. The empty sky upper centre and right easily takes the single caption. Minor: dappled leaf-light on the paving hints at moonlight despite 'no moon', and the figure is a little larger than a true wide.

Minor only: the puckered brand patch sits nearer the elbow than a hand's width above the wrist, with the thin white scar running from the wrist beside it; the room is a touch brighter than 'very dark'. Night look is right: bare chest, ribs bound in white cloth, cream shoulder cloth, cream dhoti, hair loose with no grey, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud. Palm-frond shadows fall across the wall and ceiling. The dark upper-centre wall (x 0.45-0.72, y 0.05-0.35) is clear for the caption.

Acceptable at inset size, with minor flaws. At full zoom, the left Dutch soldier (around x 0.24, y 0.42) seems to have a musket stock at his mouth, but at inset size it reads as a levelled musket. The background banners carry a small star emblem rather than plain cloth, though there is no text. The riders' olive cross-sashes are not a defined troop colour. The beat lands: cavalry drives into a blue-coat VOC line on the Colachel beach through smoke, the two central Dutch faces read clearly, and there is no blood. Smoky sky at the upper right (x 0.6-1.0, y 0-0.2) holds the caption.

Revathi is lit and fully readable instead of being only a dark shape in the doorway. This is acceptable because her balloon names her. Her braid hangs long here, while 5.4 asks for it pinned up, which is a minor continuity point. She matches her sheet (indigo sari with gold zari, jasmine braid, bead necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line, no tali). The room matches 5.1: plank door with an iron ring at the left, barred window with palms at the right, woven mat. Nagoji is off-panel in the foreground on his mat, so his tail goes to the bottom edge. The dark wall between the door and the window (x 0.47-0.75, y 0.05-0.4) and the right wall above the pots are clear for both balloons.

Framing is wider than the script's 'only her profile': it shows both figures full length, though Revathi is clearly in profile with her braid pinned up and jasmine, sitting at the mat's edge, so the beat reads. Nagoji's convalescent costume (cream dhoti, ribs bound, cream shoulder cloth, hair loose, no turban, no grey) matches 5.1. His face is on model: thick curled moustache, a flush gold stud, and a chin that is clean apart from light shading. The brand on his left forearm is pinkish rather than pale, and with his hand resting palm down on the mat it shows on the outer face of the forearm, but it reads as an old scar, not blood. Revathi has a coin necklace, armlets, a sandalwood line, no tali and no red dot. The room is right: barred window with palms, timber door, woven mat, no lamp. There is clear dark wall across the top band and between the heads for the caption and Revathi's balloon.

Clean and close to the script: two faces about a hand's width apart in the same night room as 5.4 (same door, barred window with palms, same costumes). Nagoji has his thick curled moustache, a clean chin, a small flush gold stud, loose curly hair, bound ribs and the shoulder cloth. Revathi has an indigo sari with gold, coin necklace, armlets, jasmine braid and a sandalwood line. One tiny brownish speck sits at the inner end of her brow; it is not red and is barely visible at print size. There is dark wall across the top centre and between the heads for both balloons, Nagoji on the left and Revathi on the right, in reading order.

Minor only: moonlight and bar shadows are brighter than the 'almost dark' brief, and Revathi's hairline sandalwood line is hidden by the overhead angle. Script beat is met: high view of a small room, Nagoji lying on the mat with his chest wrapped, Revathi sitting at its edge, and a night bird (owl) on a palm frond through the barred window. Nagoji is on-model (curled moustache, smooth chin, tiny gold stud, no grey, no turban). Revathi has the indigo sari, coin necklace, armlets and jasmine braid, with no red mark. The art has no text. The dark upper wall gives a large clear area for the caption.

The shot is wider than the scripted face close-up: she is a seated full figure hugging her knees, and her face is about a fifth of the frame height. That knees-hugging pose against the wall also differs from her seated pose at the mat's edge in 6.1 and 6.4. Otherwise she is on her sheet: indigo sari with gold, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets and the sandalwood line. The small dark dot between her brows matches the approved sheet and is not a red bindi. Her expression is steady and her eyes go to the dark window. There is no text, and the large dark wall in the centre takes both balloons easily.

The beat reads: a memory panel in pale, cooler daylight, a younger Revathi from behind on a laterite wall, and a distant lagoon edge with a horse among spearmen. Distance is kept and there is no gore. Minor: the horse reads as stumbling forward riderless rather than clearly going down, and the spearmen lean toward a hunt more than a melee. That is acceptable at this distance. The flag is plain cloth. She is seen from behind, so her face is not readable. The big pale sky takes the off-panel balloon.

Minor only: the pale round brand and thin white scar sit on the upper and outer face of Nagoji's LEFT forearm rather than strictly the inner face, but the arm is correct and the brand has no letters and is not a cross. There is faint stubble shading on his chin, not a beard. Script beat is met: Revathi's composed profile on the right, Nagoji's eyes on her, in the same dark room with the barred window and palms. Both match their sheets, and Revathi wears the sandalwood hairline line with no red dot. The dark central wall between them takes the caption and the long Revathi balloon without covering faces or hands.

Minor issues: (1) Revathi has a tiny extra pale vertical sandal stroke between her brows with a dark-inked tip. Pixel check shows it is dark brown or black, not red, so the widow rule (no red dot or sindoor) still holds. (2) Nagoji's outstretched forearm comes from under the cloth at the right, so the arm geometry is a little ambiguous in the shadows, though it reads as his arm laid on the mat. (3) There is light stubble shading on his chin, and the far end of his moustache droops low. Script beat is met: a close, low shot of Revathi's hand finding Nagoji's on the woven mat in the dark room, with the barred window and palms consistent with panels 1 and 4. The upper-centre dark wall (left of the window and above Nagoji's head) holds both balloons clear of faces and the hands.

Acceptable. The beat works: joined hands in the foreground, Revathi's face lifting toward Nagoji, same night room with the barred window and plank door. Nagoji has the curled moustache, a clean chin (faint shading only) and the gold stud. The brand and scar are on his near LEFT forearm, which is the correct arm. The hands read soundly and there is clear dark wall top-centre for both balloons. Problems to note: (1) He wears a long-sleeved cream shirt with the sleeves pushed up. The script's night look is cream dhoti, ribs bound and a cream shoulder cloth, which panel 7.3 needs. This matches 6.5 but not 7.3. If strict costume consistency is wanted, regenerate with the shirt replaced by a bare chest, rib bandage and a draped cream shoulder cloth. (2) There is grey at his temples. The ch16 bible row allows it, but the script's 4.1 and 5.1 say no grey for this sequence. (3) The brand sits nearer the elbow than a hand's width above the wrist. This is minor.

Clean. Revathi is close, in the same room with the barred window, palms and plank door. She matches her sheet: indigo sari with gold zari, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line and no tali. There is no text. Both balloons have clear space on the plain wall between her head and the window, and under the window. The scene is a little brighter than 'what light there is', which is acceptable.

Forced pick (past the two-correction rule; v04 is a hand retouch). Faults for the author: (1) Key beat only partly shown: Nagoji's hand does not close on Revathi's wrist. A male hand grips his own upper arm just below her bangled wrist, and its arm comes from behind his arm on her side. It is unclear whose hand it is: it reads as his far-side left hand reaching across, or as a stray third hand. His near (right) arm hangs straight down with the hand resting on his lap. (2) The lighting is too bright and warm for midnight with no lamp. Both faces and his torso are evenly lit as if by a lamp, not by the faint glow from the barred window with deep shadow around them. (3) A light stubble shadow on Nagoji's chin and jaw: minor, but the bible says clean-shaven, smooth skin. (4) Revathi's fingers already rest on top of his shoulder, not tracing up the arm past the bandage edge. Acceptable, but less of a 'tracing' motion. (5) Her hair is loose and curly around her face, softer than the neat sheet hairline. Her bell jhumka earrings match her sheet. Correct: Nagoji has a thick curled moustache, a tiny flush gold stud, no grey, no turban, and a rib bandage plus a slipped shoulder cloth. Revathi has an indigo and gold sari, a jasmine braid, a flat-coin necklace, armlets and a sandalwood line, with no red dot. The room has a barred window, palms, a timber door and a mat, with no bed and no text. There is clear dark wall space for Nagoji's balloon above his head (about x 0.46 to 0.73, y 0.02 to 0.16) or on the wall right of his head below the window.

Small issues only. Nagoji now sits up cross-legged, where in 7.3 he was reclining, and they sit about an arm's length apart. The beat still reads: his right hand holds her wrist and her hand hangs relaxed, so she has not pulled away. Both hands and both of his arms are sound. He has a thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, rib bandage, slipped shoulder cloth and no grey. Revathi wears the indigo sari with jasmine, coin necklace and armlets, and her only forehead mark is the sandalwood line. It is the same barred-window room. The open dark wall between his head and the window takes both of Revathi's balloons.

Small issues only. The framing is a medium shot rather than a true close-up. Between Revathi's brows there is a dark speck of 1 to 2 pixels: it is not red and cannot be seen at reading size. Nagoji's lobe ornament is a slightly oval gold bead, but it sits flush with nothing hanging from it. His dark bare shoulder and long curly hair fill the foreground and he has no turban. She lifts her chin, defiant, in the same room as 7.4 (window at left, door at right). There is clear dark wall above her face for both speeches. The bottom-right floor holds the separate lower caption, overlapping at most the sari hem. Nagoji is seen from behind, so his tail points to where his hidden mouth would be.

Minor only. There is a small muted rust-brown stain on Nagoji's rib binding at his side. It reads as a dried old dressing (aftermath, not gore), in line with earlier chapters' precedent, but the bandages in 8.3 and 8.4 are clean. The brand on his left forearm is a pale puckered patch with faint radial ridges, sitting mid-forearm, with a faint thin line toward the elbow; it is not legible and not a cross. Otherwise clean. Revathi walks a half step ahead and leads him by the hand, glancing back. He holds his bound side. Both are barefoot. He is in dhoti, rib binding and cream shoulder cloth, with no turban and no grey, plus the thick curled moustache, clean chin and small gold stud. She has indigo sari with gold, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, armlets, sandalwood line and no tali. The dark granary has clay vessels taller than the waist, sacks, beams and the plank door at right. No text and no lettering needed.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Minor only. There is a woven basket and a pot in the cellar corners. The brand patch shows on the visible face of his left forearm, which may be the outer rather than the inner side. Otherwise clean: earth cellar, single mat, Revathi kneeling and striking flint so the brass lamp catches, indigo sari with blouse and pallu, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, armlets, sandalwood line, no tali. Nagoji stoops in the low doorway behind her in dhoti, rib binding and shoulder cloth, with moustache, clean chin and small gold stud. The large plain earth wall at upper right is free for her long balloon.

The script says standing, but they sit close together on the mat. The emotional beat is intact (close, small lamplight, both dressed as before) and it suits his injured ribs. The brass lamp sits on the floor by the door rather than on the mat where she lit it in 8.3. The brand and scar sit higher on his left forearm, toward the elbow. There is light stubble texture on Nagoji's chin, within tolerance. Faces, his moustache and gold stud, and her blouse, sari, pallu, jasmine braid, coin necklace and armlets are correct. The wide dark earth wall above both heads takes all three balloons.

Minor only. Revathi has a tiny dark (not red) tick between her brows below the sandalwood line, barely visible at print size. The lamp is a tall brass stand lamp, matching 8.6 rather than the small lamp of 8.3 and 8.4. The brand and white scar sit toward the elbow, consistent with the 8.4 pick. Otherwise clean. Revathi sits on the mat with both arms raised, unpinning her hair, which falls in long dark waves past her shoulders. She is fully dressed in the indigo sari with the pallu over her shoulder, with jasmine, flat-coin necklace and armlets. Nagoji is bare-chested with rib binding, cream shoulder cloth and dhoti, no grey, his 3/4 face watching her: thick curled moustache, clean chin, small flush gold stud. The cellar has an earth wall, beams, a mat and a plank door, with no text. The caption fits on the plain earth wall at top centre between her raised elbow and his hair (about x 0.46 to 0.64, y 0.03 to 0.25), clear of both faces and her hands.

Minor: the foreground lamp is a taller brass stand lamp than the small lamp in 8.3. Both are brass oil lamps with open wicks, so it is acceptable. The two clothed silhouettes merging on the wall are the intended implied beat. There is no text or nudity. The upper-left wall between the lamp and the shadows and the right wall above the mat are clear for the two captions.

Minor only. They are propped against the wall rather than lying flat on the mat, but the embrace reads clearly: her head is on his shoulder, he holds his ribs, and she can sit up from this in 9.3. Nagoji matches the script costume: bare chest, white rib binding, plain cream shoulder cloth, dhoti, loose hair, no grey, flush ear stud and thick moustache. There is faint stubble shading on his chin. The brand and the long scar show on the upper face of his palm-down left forearm, mid-forearm. That is technically the outer side, but it is small and incidental. Revathi matches her sheet with the pallu over her shoulder and no tali. The upper right wall is clear for both balloons.

Shows the beat well: Nagoji reclined on the mat, mid-laugh and wincing, his hand clutching the rib binding. Costume matches 9.1 (dhoti, rib binding, shoulder cloth over the left shoulder, hair loose), with the same cellar, tall brass lamp and door. There is clear dark wall at upper right and upper left for both balloons. Revathi is off-panel to the right, on his shoulder-cloth side as in 9.1, so her tail goes to the right edge. Minor flaws: a small cluster of silvery strands above his ear (about x 0.24-0.26, y 0.25-0.28) goes against the no-grey rule for page 9, and the chin and jaw carry light stubble shading. Both are small in an inset panel and read as highlight and shadow, but retouch the grey strands if possible. v01 is not a listed candidate; it also has a painted inset and the wrong tunic and sash costume.

Clean. Revathi sits up, adjusting the sari at her shoulder, looking down at the reclining Nagoji with a serious expression. She matches her sheet and the bible: indigo and gold sari with the pallu over her shoulder, jasmine braid, gold bead necklace, jhumkas, armlets, a sandalwood line at the hairline, and no red dot or tali. Nagoji matches 9.2 in costume (dhoti, binding, shoulder cloth), with a clean chin (faint shading only), a flush gold stud and no grey. Same cellar, tall lamp and door as 9.1 and 9.2. Hands are sound. The large plain wall between and above them gives room for both of Revathi's balloons.

Clean. Revathi matches her sheet: indigo sari with the pallu over her shoulder, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line, and no tali or red dot. She wears a small private smile and glances to the right, toward where Nagoji lay in 9.3. The same cellar door and timber ceiling show. The lamp is a tall standing brass lamp rather than the small one in 9.1. That is a minor difference and is acceptable in a close-up background. The upper right wall between her head and the door is clear for both balloons. Nagoji is off-panel to the right.

Shows the beat: Nagoji alone, sitting up on the mat and looking at the low door, with dawn in thin blades through its cracks. The brass lamp is out with one thread of smoke rising, and the other half of the mat is empty. Minor drift: a few faint grey strands at the temple (no grey is wanted on page 9). His shoulder cloth has a gold border, where 9.1 has a plain one. The rib binding is hidden under the draped cloth. The brand sits high near the elbow on the visible face of the forearm, small at panel scale. The large plain wall in the upper middle holds both captions.

Clean. A close strip of Nagoji's bare forearm and hand resting palm-down on the empty mat, with dhoti at left, beside a cold low brass bowl lamp with a burnt-out wick. Thin dawn light comes through the cracks of the low door. The lamp matches the burned-out bowl lamp in 9.5. The hand is sound: four fingers visible, thumb tucked. No face is shown, and the upper mud wall gives a wide low-detail band for the long caption. v01 is not a listed candidate; its lamp is still lit and the sleeve is wrong.

Minor only. The round-2 correction landed. Varma has jet-black hair in a knot, no grey, no earring and no jewels, and wears a plain white cloth over his left shoulder, so any dressing is hidden. He has a namam and a curled moustache and no longer reads as Nagoji. Nagoji matches his sheet and the 10.4 costume: barefoot, rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves pushed up, red sash, thick curled moustache, clean chin, no grey, a pale patch on the inner left forearm, and no boots or talwar. Small deviations: Nagoji's gold stud has a tiny second bead under it, which reads as a stud at panel size. There is a faint pale highlight at the centre of his forehead. Varma's knot carries a thin gold-beaded band. The scene matches the script: wet mossy steps, clear river over stone, brass ghee lamps along the granite wall, tiled roofs and morning light, with no gopuram and no text. The open sky at upper right holds both captions clear of faces.

Minor only. The left-shoulder dressing is not visible because it is the far shoulder under the cloth, which reads as 'half hidden'. There is a faint touch of grey at Varma's sideburn. The tall brass lamp stands read slightly like candles. The beat is clear: barefoot, no crown or jewels, plain white cloth, gold and pepper sacks laid before the dark inner shrine. The dark upper-left hall gives clean caption space.

Minor only. The round-2 correction landed. Varma wears no necklaces, his face is mature with a curled moustache and the red-and-white Vaishnavite mark, and the sword is a long straight blade with a plain gilt hilt (round pommel, short straight guard, dark grip) that matches 10.4. The priest matches the V13 sheet: curly hair in a knot, white forehead lines with a red dot, sacred thread, and a gold-bordered white cloth. He carries the sword on both palms, grip in one hand and blade on the other, into Varma's cupped hands. The hands are sound. Small deviations: Varma's hair is loose curls in a low bun, not the sleek side knot of the sheet, but it sits between 10.2 (low knot) and 10.4 (curls with a topknot). He has a pin-sized ear stud and light stubble. The left-shoulder dressing is not visible because his near left shoulder is under the white cloth, which reads as half hidden. The sanctum glow shows a tiered lamp-stand, not a deity, and there is no text. The dark ceiling band at top centre (about x 0.37 to 0.74, y 0 to 0.09) and the dark stone at upper left hold the medium caption clear of faces and of the hand-over.

Minor only. Varma keeps the pearl drop earrings from his sheet and has a gold border on his white cloth, and the narrow linen dressing on his left shoulder is not clearly separate from the draped cloth. Kayal shows a faint pale hair highlight on her forehead, not a real marking. Both captions fit in the open sky in the top centre and top right, between Nagoji's turban and Varma's head and to the right of Varma. Nagoji is correct: thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny flush gold stud, no grey, red turban and sash, and he watches Varma. Varma is bare-headed with no crest, and the sword lies across his knees. The setting is green paddy country with a red-earth track and a plain-dress column behind. There is no painted text.

It hits the scripted beat: a 3:1 strip where the bare straight sword across Varma's white-clad knees is the subject, with a sun flare on its edge, and the small column of riders behind on the red track through wet paddy and palms. Varma's dark, black-maned horse matches 10.4, his face is out of frame, the hands are sound, there is no text, and clear blue sky at upper right takes the caption. Minor points. The lead escort rider, in a rust turban and cream tunic, has a short black beard and rides a bay with a white blaze and white socks, so a close reader could take him as a bearded Nagoji on the wrong horse. He is tiny (face about 40 px high), and a second rider also wears a saffron turban, so he reads as escort. A touch-up (white turban or clean chin) is worth considering. The sword's guard is a small lozenge rather than the plain straight bar of 10.3. Small white pennons on two spears are not war banners.

Minor: Lannoy stands just behind Ramayyan at the table rather than clearly apart beside it, and has a faint white rim outline. Both principals match their sheets (Lannoy in white tunic-coat over white mundu, not blue). Caption space: open sky top centre-right (x 0.62-0.88, y 0-0.15) and wall above the awning top-left.

Framing departs from the script: Nagoji is a large over-the-shoulder foreground figure on the left rather than a small figure on a bastion lip, and he looks across more than down. The high angle over angled, sloped star-trace bastions (under construction, matching the half-built parapet in 11.4) still carries the beat. Nagoji matches: rust-red turban, red sash, thick moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, no grey. Caption space: the sky band along the top (x 0.22-1.0, y 0-0.08) and the low-detail parapet stones bottom-left (x 0-0.45, y 0.86-1.0). The 11.3 inset can sit top-right over the distant landscape.
Clean. Tall square-cornered Deccan fort on a crag in dry ochre colours. The unlettered saffron swallow-tailed pennant suits a memory panel. Wide open sky top-left for the caption.

Clean. Lannoy matches his sheet (white tunic-coat, white mundu, sandals, pale hair with a black ribbon) and is kneeling, tracing angled lines in wet clay with a stick. The squat, heavy mason ponders the sketch. The clay drawing has no letters. Open sky top centre-right (x 0.42-0.98, y 0-0.13) holds both Lannoy balloons.

Minor only. The clay sketch on the slab is a plain grid rather than the star trace drawn in 11.4. Lannoy is brushing dust off his thighs and mundu rather than his knees exactly. Otherwise it is clean. Lannoy matches his sheet: pale curly hair with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals, no blue coat. The mason is the same one as in 11.4 (beard, headband, striped shoulder cloth) and rests his hand on the old wall with an unconvinced look. The setting is the same parapet. There is no painted text, and hands and anatomy are sound. Open sky fills the upper frame above both men for the MASON and LANNOY balloons.

Clean. Lannoy matches his sheet: pale wavy hair with a black ribbon, white stand-collar tunic-coat over a white mundu, sandals. He stands before a line of bare-chested Nair musketeers in dhotis drilling with upright muskets, with a cannon crew beyond. Hands are sound and there is no text. The plain white flag carries no emblem. Open sky across the top centre and right gives room for both Lannoy lines.

Accepted with one minor fault logged. Nagoji's ear ornament is a single gold bead about 4 to 5 px across, sitting right at the bottom edge of the lobe (around x 765, y 207 at native size). The r2 v02 had a stud with a separate drop hanging below it. v03 has one bead and no second piece, so the r2 ear correction mostly worked. The bead still sits just under the lobe line rather than flush on it, which matches the r2 plan to accept the ear after one more try, as was done in ch9 and ch11. Everything else is clean. Nagoji has a thick curled moustache, a clean chin and jaw, black hair with no grey (page 12), a rust-red turban, a cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, a red sash, cream trousers and boots, and a talwar raised in his right hand while his left hand holds the reins. Megha is a dappled grey with a black mane and tail at full gallop, and her anatomy is sound. The troop of Travancore horse wheels around him with raised talwars. The bearded riders in turbans and sashes match the neighbouring panels and r2. The setting fits 12.1 and 12.3: laterite fort wall, timber dais, palms, a thin band of sea and one tiny ship at anchor. There is no painted text, blood or anachronism. The wide upper-right sky leaves clear space for both the Nagoji balloon and the caption.

Acceptable with minor notes. Nagoji is on the sheet: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, no grey, red sash, boots, talwar. Lannoy is in the white coat and mundu, looking down and tracing rectangles in the dust with his toe. He wears sandals (the bible's 16-23 row) rather than the script's 'boot'. A tiny pale twig shows at his toe. With the arms crossed, the brand reads on the left forearm, but nearer the elbow than a hand's width above the wrist, and the long white scar is not shown. The background musketeers wear white tunics, trousers, boots and turbans, unlike 12.1's bare-chested Nairs in dhotis. Lannoy speaks first but stands to the right of Nagoji, so the letterer should stack Lannoy's balloon higher in the open sky at upper right and Nagoji's below it.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Acceptable with minor notes. Lannoy is breaking into a laugh, hand on hip, in the white coat and mundu with pale hair and a black ribbon. Nagoji stands beside him with arms crossed and a wry look, matching the face lock: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, no grey. A knot of soldiers behind watches, some amused. Hands are sound and there is no text. The brand and scar sit on the top (left) forearm, but nearer the elbow than a hand's width above the wrist. A small wooden frame of two posts and a crossbeam on the wall at right loosely recalls a gallows, but it has no rope or noose. The background soldiers wear cream tunics, blue turbans, cross-belts and boots, unlike 12.1's bare-chested Nairs. Open sky across the top centre and right holds the three balloons.

Clean. Varma in V13 court dress with crest, necklaces and spear, pointing over the pass. Ramayyan with palm-leaf bundle and stylus. Lannoy in white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals. Nagoji: rust-red turban, red sash, curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud. Hands are sound and there is no text. Open sky at top right holds both Varma lines. Note: Nagoji shows no grey here, but the ch16 bible row asks for first grey at the temples (the script says 'no grey yet'), and panels 2 and 5 show grey. The author needs to settle which is right; I did not resolve it.

Acceptable. Minor points: (1) Framing is a medium two-shot, not a true close on Varma with Nagoji at the frame edge, but Varma's sideways look at Nagoji reads clearly. (2) Nagoji has first grey at the temple, which follows the ch16 bible row but not the script's 'no grey yet', and panels 1 and 4 show none. (3) The brand and the thin white scar are correctly on the pushed-up LEFT forearm, but the brand sits mid-forearm (the wrist is off-frame). No text. Hands are sound. Sky at top centre holds the line.

Minor only. Varma's blue bundle has rich gold borders, so it reads as a finer cloth than the rough blue drill coats of 13.4. Varma wears sandals, and his knot sits high at the back of his head rather than plainly above the left ear. Everything else fits: all three principals match their sheets. Nagoji has a clean chin, a flush gold stud, no grey and arms folded. De Lannoy is in his white coat, mundu and sandals. Varma is bare-chested and bare-headed in a cream mundu with gold necklaces and black hair. Dutch hulls are small on the horizon, there is no painted text, the hands are sound, and the open sky in the upper right takes Varma's balloon.

Acceptable, and the panel has no lettering. Lannoy, still in his white coat and mundu, lifts a short blue coat with brass buttons from a growing pile of coats and stiff felt tricornes. The men around him look sour. Nagoji has his arms folded and is on model: rust-red turban, clean chin, gold stud, no grey. Minor: the surrounding men already wear blue sleeveless waistcoats, and the background ranks wear blue vests and caps, which slightly blunts the 'only the pile is blue' beat. Nagoji's folded forearms show no brand; acceptable, since the inner forearms are turned in. No text. Hands are sound.

Forced pick (hand-retouched v04). Faults for the author: (1) Nagoji has a clear streak of grey hair at the temple below the turban, but on page 13 he should have no grey yet. (2) His ear stud is a round gold bead, a little larger and more prominent than the tiny flush stud, though nothing hangs from it. (3) There is faint stubble-like texture shading on his jaw and chin. It does not read as a beard, but it is not perfectly smooth. (4) Blue coats show up early. The page 13 beat is that the blue Company coats are only now being unfolded (13.4), yet a background officer at right wears a full blue coat with a red sash, the dais figures wear blue coats and caps, and every infantryman has a blue sash. (5) The background infantry wear white trousers and boots instead of dhotis and bare feet, which jars with page 14. (6) The background firing line aims roughly toward the left foreground, where the two principals stand. Fortunately it is distant and blurred. (7) The 'dais' at left is a tall two-storey timber stand with bearded onlookers, not a small timber dais. (8) The ship on the horizon is small and at anchor, so it is acceptable per 13.3. Good points: Lannoy matches his sheet (pale wavy hair with black ribbon, white high-collared tunic-coat, bare-headed, hands behind back), the cupped-hand whisper beat is clear, and the brand and scar sit on the raised inner LEFT forearm. There is no painted text, and anatomy is sound. Lettering space: clear sky at the upper centre-left above Nagoji's turban (about x 0.28-0.45, y 0.0-0.09) and a broad clear sky band at upper right (x 0.62-1.0, y 0.0-0.24). Tails run to Nagoji's mouth behind his cupped hand.

Clean. Lannoy matches his sheet: pale curly hair tied with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals, and he gestures at the infantry. The infantry are bare-chested in hitched dhotis with muskets on their shoulders. Nagoji has his arms crossed, unconvinced, in the rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, boots and talwar, with a clean chin, a small gold stud and no grey. The conch banner carries no text, and the ship is only a tiny hull on the horizon. There is a large clear sky at upper right for both Lannoy balloons and the caption.

Acceptable with minor notes. Nagoji rides at the head and flank of the line rather than strictly behind it. The stiff plumed caps read slightly like later shakos, but the script asks for stiff hats and panel 14.3 matches them. Varma on the dais is a little larger than 'small in the distance'. Otherwise the panel is on beat: Nagoji on a grey horse with a black mane (Megha), blue drill coat with the collar tight, rust-red turban on, clean chin, gold stud and no grey. Varma wears the cream-and-gold turban with the peacock crest, which is correct for the dais. The infantry wear blue coats over dhotis and are barefoot, with their muskets at one angle. There are drummers and a conch-on-red banner with no text, and the ship is only a tiny hull on the horizon. The upper-right sky is clear for the long caption.

v03 fixes what failed in r1 and r2. Nagoji's temples are fully black with no grey. His sleeves are down, so no brand shows. The men's hats are the same tall, plumed, dark blue hats with brass badges as in panel 14.2, now held in hands or pushed back, and there are no tricornes. Nagoji matches the commander sheet: rust-red turban, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, red sash, cream trousers, boots and talwar, with the blue drill coat open over his clothes. The fall-out beat reads clearly: coats open over bare chests, dhotis loosened, men grinning up at him. The setting (drill ground, laterite wall, palms, thin band of sea) and the daylight match panel 14.2. There is no text and no gore, and the hands are sound. Open sky across the top centre (x 0.25 to 0.6, y 0 to 0.2) gives the caption room without touching any face. Minor issues: at high zoom the ear ornament looks like a stud with a tiny second bead just below the lobe, but at reading size it reads as a small gold stud. The seated soldier at left centre has long curly black hair and a curled moustache, but he has no turban, no ear stud and no grey, and he sits among the men, so he reads as a soldier, not a second Nagoji. Several standing men look up at the sky rather than at Nagoji, but the seated men's eyelines carry the beat.

Acceptable. Revathi matches her sheet: indigo sari with gold, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, armlets, sandalwood line, and no tali. Nagoji matches the commander look and the bible: rust-red turban, red sash, thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, and faint first grey at the temples, as the script asks from 14.4. The Velinadu muster is right: bare-chested men in white mundus with no coats, firing in turn from standing and kneeling ranks, under the red banner with the silver conch. Revathi looks toward the formations, not at him. Minor points: the two stand close side by side rather than at an obviously formal distance. The brand shows on the top of his crossed forearm. The conch has some faint interior shading but no lettering. Lettering space on the left is tight. Put Revathi's balloon in the sky above her head (top left). Put Nagoji's balloon in the sky between his turban and the flag. The caption fits in the open sky at upper right or as a slim box along the top-left edge. None of these needs to cover a face.

Clean. Revathi is close and matches her sheet: indigo sari with gold zari, a jasmine braid, the flat-coin necklace, gold armlets and the sandalwood line at the hairline. She has no tali and no red dot. The warm tone in her hair parting matches her approved sheet and does not read as sindoor. Gun smoke drifts behind her. Bare-chested infantry in white mundus fire under the conch-on-red banner on the red earth, with the Kovilakam roofs in the distance, which is consistent with panel 14.4. A small second pale line sits mid-forehead, which is minor. The upper-right sky is clear for both balloons.

Accepted with minor notes. The beat reads well: a line of young recruits in white sleeveless tunics and white mundus, crossed leather belts, blue waistbands and white turbans, barefoot, bringing flintlocks to the shoulder. This matches the bible's Travancore regulars. The flag on the right is a large plain white flag, not the Travancore standard (silver conch on red), and could read as a surrender flag. A tiny figure on the pavilion wears a rust-red turban and may have a dark chin, so it could be mistaken for Nagoji. There is no text, gore or anachronism, and the hands hold up at this scale. Wide open sky across the top middle has room for both captions.

This one is acceptable and fixes everything wrong with r1. Nagoji matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, grey at the temples, an unreadable guarded face, and commander dress (rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves rolled, broad red sash, boots, talwar). The recruits continue panel 15.1: barefoot, white tunics and mundus, blue waistbands, crossed belts, flintlocks raised in one line on sand. Background officers wear white turbans and pale coats. There are no flags, no smoke and no clone of Nagoji's look. The upper-right sky is clear for the caption. Minor flaws: (1) The starburst brand sits correctly on his lower (LEFT) crossed forearm, but a thin pale scar streak runs ACROSS the upper (RIGHT) forearm. The bible puts that scar along the left forearm, wrist to elbow. It is small at page size; a retouch could remove it. (2) Tiny engraving squiggles on the musket lock plates cannot be read at print size. (3) The temple grey is a little stronger than 'faint', but it matches the picks for 15.4 and 15.6.

Accepted with minor notes. The memory is in dry Deccan colours: black soil, a man in a white pagdi and angarkha walking the field with a hoe, mesas and tiled village houses. In the doorway are the father (white-haired, bent, white pheta, black wool kambal, coarse dhoti, staff) and the mother (white hair, green glass bangles, turmeric-yellow hands). The mother's sari falls as a straight skirt and is not clearly the bible's kashta drape. The field man has a short beard rather than Bhalerao's thin young moustache, but his face is turned away and tiny. There is no text and the hands hold up. The open sky at upper left has room for both captions, even at inset size.

Accepted with minor notes. Nagoji matches his sheet: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, grey at the temples. Dhanaji matches his: white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short black beard, small gold hoop, talwar. They lean on a low laterite wall at night above a lamplit drill ground, and all four hands rest soundly on the stone. The small background musketeers wear blue coats with baggy white trousers and dark footwear, where the script asks for dhotis and bare feet. They also differ from the white-clad 15.1 recruits, though it is a different, night company. The wooden structure behind them is a watch platform with no rope or noose. The lamps are open flames, not glass. The starry sky at upper right is clear for both balloons.

This one is acceptable and fixes everything wrong with r1. It is a closer chest-up two-shot of both men leaning on the same laterite wall as 15.4, at night, with blue-coated musketeers loading by open-flame lamps below. Dhanaji is on the left, as in 15.6: white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short black beard, small gold hoop, stockier build, squinting sideways at Nagoji. Nagoji wears commander dress with no blue coat: rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves rolled, red sash, talwar hilt. He has the thick curled moustache, clean chin, tiny gold stud and grey at the temple. All four hands rest soundly on the stone. There is no text, and the ship is only a tiny shape on the horizon. Minor flaws: (1) Nagoji's hooded eyes look level and to the left, past Dhanaji, rather than clearly down at the lamps. The guarded beat still reads. (2) Light stubble shading shows on his jaw, but the chin reads clean-shaven against Dhanaji's beard. (3) The space for balloons is the dark sky band at the top and the gap between the two turbans (about x 0.33 to 0.60, y 0 to 0.25). The three balloons will fit there but are tight and may overlap the tops of the turbans, never a face.

Accepted with minor notes. Dhanaji laughs and waves a hand, with drawn head-shake motion arcs (not text). He matches his sheet: white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short black beard, gold hoop. Nagoji, with the corner of his mouth lifting, matches his: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, clean chin, gold stud, grey at the temples. The hands hold up. The pair read as being at ground level on the drill ground rather than at the low wall of 15.4, a small continuity drift. The background infantry wear blue coats with trousers and boots rather than dhotis and bare feet. One tiny bearded figure on the pavilion at far right wears a reddish turban. The dark sky between and around the two heads is clear for both balloons.

Minor: Nagoji's ear ornament is drawn as a tiny two-bead drop instead of the flush gold stud from the 2026-10-02 author decision. It is only about 11 px tall in this wide shot, so a quick retouch to a flush stud is advised. Otherwise it is clean: dusk bastion over the inlet with boats below; Nagoji has the rust turban, sash, cream tunic and trousers, boots, talwar, a clean chin and a faint white scar on the outer left forearm; Lannoy is bare-headed with pale hair, white tunic-coat, mundu and sandals; hands are sound; there is no text. The figures are lit rather than in true silhouette, but both read clearly. A large pewter-and-orange sky across the top half gives room for all three lines.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Minor only. Nagoji's head-shake is shown as a sceptical sidelong look with folded arms rather than a literal shake, which still reads as the beat. The grey at his right temple is a little stronger than 'faint' but stays at the temple. Otherwise clean: his chin is clean-shaven, the gold ear stud is small and flush, and the brand stays hidden. Lannoy matches his sheet (pale hair with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat over a mundu) and turns to Nagoji with a thin smile. The bastion, parapet, cannon, inlet with Marakkar boats and dusk light match 16.1 and 16.2. No painted text, and the hands are sound. The open dusk sky in the upper left and top centre leaves room for Lannoy's three speeches.

Minor only. Nagoji's grey at the temple is slightly stronger than 'faint'. A small domed sentry turret on the far left was not in 16.1 or 16.2 but fits the fort. Otherwise clean: Nagoji leans with his forearms on the parapet, with a clean chin, curled moustache, flush gold stud, rust-red turban, red sash and boots. Lannoy stands beside him in profile, eyes on the water, in his white coat, mundu and sandals with his hands behind his back. The room, light and costumes match the neighbouring panels. No painted text, and the anatomy is sound. Open sky across the top centre and upper right leaves room for both balloons.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Clean. Lannoy matches his sheet (pale hair with a black ribbon, white tunic-coat and mundu) and is turning a stone chip at dusk on the parapet. Nagoji is cropped at the left edge as the script asks, with a curled moustache, clean chin (only faint shading), gold stud and grey temples. The open sky at upper right takes both balloons.

Minor only. The faint grey at Nagoji's temples does not show under the turban. His ear stud is a small round bead, but it sits on the lobe with nothing hanging from it. The sunset is warmer than 'old pewter', but it matches the orange dusk of 17.1 and 17.4. Otherwise clean: Lannoy (pale hair with black ribbon, white tunic-coat, mundu, sandals) has his arm still extended after the throw and the stone arcs over the water. Nagoji stands to the left, as in 17.1, in rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, boots and talwar, with a thick moustache and a clean chin, watching the stone. The cannon embrasure is on the laterite parapet. Hands are sound and there is no text. Open sky at the upper middle and upper right leaves room for both balloons.

Minor only. The square glass ink bottle looks slightly modern. The rendering is more painterly than inked. Otherwise clean: a pale-haired boy of about ten works at a wooden desk in a whitewashed schoolroom with leaded windows and cold grey light. He draws a star-shaped fortress with compasses and a ruler. The plan is only lines and angles, with no people and no writing or numerals, and the ruler carries no markings. The only figure is the boy, and the grown De Lannoy is absent. Hands are sound. The plain grey wall between the window and the crucifix, and above the coat rack, leaves clear room for both off-panel balloons.

Acceptable, with minor notes. Lannoy has turned to Nagoji with an open palm toward the parapet and fort, and the last light falls between them. Nagoji matches his sheet (clean chin, grey temples, gold stud) and stands with his arms crossed. On his LEFT forearm, the brand sits mid-forearm toward the elbow on the visible outer side, not a hand's width above the wrist on the inner side, and the white scar runs diagonally across the forearm instead of lengthwise. Both are small at panel scale, and the brand is a blurred patch, not a cross or letters. The sun sits just above the horizon, slightly earlier than in 17.2. Three balloons fit in the sky above and between the heads.

Clean. A dim Flemish Gothic church: an elderly grey-haired woman in a dark fringed shawl lights a candle with a taper at a side altar, before an iron rack of votive flames, with a Madonna statue above. There is no text, the hand is sound, and nothing is anachronistic. The dark upper-left vault and window wall hold both off-panel lines without covering her face or the candles.

Minor only: at close zoom Nagoji's gold ear ornament has a tiny bead under the lobe stud, so it reads almost like a small drop, though at reading size it is a small gold stud. The grey at his temple is a little stronger than 'faint'. His crossed arms hide the inner-left-forearm brand and scar, which is acceptable because they are not called for in this beat. Otherwise it is clean. Lannoy matches his sheet (pale curly hair with black ribbon, white tunic-coat, mundu, sandals) and turns from the water toward Nagoji with a hand on the parapet. Nagoji (rust turban, curled moustache, smooth chin, cream tunic, red sash, boots) faces him squarely. The setting is a laterite bastion with a cannon embrasure in the last light, with small sailing boats on the inlet. There is no text, and the hands are sound. Both lower corners are open floor for the 18.2 inset, and the sky between and to the right of the heads is wide and clear for four lettering areas.

Minor: where the rope fails, near the hull, the frayed strands bunch into a lump that could, looked at closely, be read as a small knot. At inset size it reads as the wet, fraying break the script asks for. The line is otherwise straight and taut and runs out of frame at top right, with no loop or noose. The hand is anatomically sound and slips from the line in a torn grey-brown sleeve (Keshavrao's colour). There is no face, no figure, no blood and no text, and the cold storm palette is right.

Minor only. The background Nair guards carry spears and wear their topknots on the crown rather than tied forward. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small gold bead rather than a perfectly flush stud, the same as in the accepted page 16 and 17 frames. Everything the beat needs is present: Udayagiri's granite hill, the new angled bastions, the wall walk, the ditch, and scrub with one small muzzle flash and puff of smoke at right. Lannoy (white coat and mundu, sandals) points along the wall and Nagoji (rust-red turban, commander dress, clean chin, faint grey) walks beside him. The large dusk sky at upper right leaves clear room for both captions. No text, and the hands are sound. The frame is 1536 px wide; as the script notes, it needs a 2x upscale to reach 300 PPI at full width.

Framing is a chest-up close shot rather than truly tight on the ear. The lifting strand is a few loose locks trailing off the far side of his head, where his hidden right ear is, which is subtle but readable with 18.3 and 18.5 on either side. His sidelong, half-startled look fits 'not yet understood'. Lannoy matches his sheet (pale wavy hair with black ribbon, long nose, white stand-collar tunic-coat). The background guards are bare-chested here but wear sleeveless white tunics in 18.3, a small inconsistency in incidental figures. No text, no gore.

Minor. The spray of stone chips bursts from the parapet top level with Nagoji's shoulder, not near his knee as scripted; it still clearly shows a shot striking the parapet beside him. A plain white pennant flies on the wall at upper left. It has no text but could faintly suggest a flag of truce, and it does not appear in 18.3. Otherwise sound. Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean chin, curled moustache, gold stud, faint grey) drags Lannoy (white coat, mundu, sandals) down behind the parapet. The hands are anatomically correct, and the outer left forearm correctly shows no brand. The sky above and right of the turban gives room for the short 'Down!' balloon without covering a face.

Clean. Sentries snatching muskets, dogs barking, torches running for the ditch, empty scrub beyond, night falling. The alarm is blown on a horn rather than a whistle, which reads the same. No text, blood or anachronism. The open sky at upper right is clear for the caption.
